List a style's layers, or preview a filter

Source: R/layer_utils.R
list_layers.Rd

The layers of a style in drawing order: their id (what layers matches), type (symbol layers are the labels labels keeps or drops), source_layer (the vector tile layer drawn; NA for background and raster layers) and feature (what features matches). With layers, labels or features, the layers a render with those filters draws; no rows when they leave nothing. Python: basemapper.list_layers().

Usage

list_layers(
  style,
  auth_token = NULL,
  layers = NULL,
  labels = TRUE,
  features = NULL
)

Arguments

style

A style (anything basemap() takes).

auth_token

Optional access token for the style URL.

layers, labels, features

Filters to preview, as the renderers take them (see basemap()).

Value

A data frame with columns id, type, source_layer and feature.

Details

A layer's feature comes from its source layer, with tables for the OpenMapTiles (OpenFreeMap, Stadia, MapTiler), Protomaps (CARTO) and Shortbread (VersaTiles) schemas and keywords for others (Esri's descriptive names, layer ids). The features are background, water, landcover, parks, buildings, roads, rail, boundaries, places, poi, terrain and other. They are a convenience: check them here, and use layers for exact control.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
list_layers("OpenFreeMap.Positron")
list_layers("OpenFreeMap.Positron", labels = "only")      # what would be drawn
list_layers("OpenFreeMap.Positron", layers = "highway_*")
} # }
